subject: Biology
text: Name two components of a balanced diet.
sets: Human nutrition

subject: Biology
text: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
explain: Carbohydrates are broken down during respiration to release energy.
sets: Human nutrition

subject: Biology
text: What is the main function of proteins in the diet?
sets: Proteins are needed to build and repair body tissues.

subject: Biology
text: Lipids provide more energy per gram than carbohydrates.
sets: Lipids release approximately twice as much energy per gram as carbohydrates.

subject: Biology
text: A lack of vitamin C can cause the deficiency disease ___.
sets: Vitamin C is needed for healthy connective tissue and wound healing. Its deficiency causes scurvy.

subject: Biology
text: Which mineral is required to make haemoglobin in red blood cells?
explain: Iron is needed to produce haemoglobin
sets: which transports oxygen in the blood.

subject: Biology
text: What is the role of dietary fibre in the digestive system?
answer: adds bulk to faeces|helps food move through the gut|prevents constipation
sets: Fibre adds bulk to faeces and helps maintain peristalsis

subject: Biology
text: State one function of water in the human body.
answer: solvent for chemical reactions|transport of substances|temperature regulation|component of body fluids
sets: Water acts as a solvent and is important for transport and temperature regulation.

subject: Biology
text: A person's energy requirement is affected by their level of physical activity.
sets: More physical activity generally increases the energy needed for muscle contraction and respiration.

subject: Biology
text: State two factors other than physical activity that affect a person's energy requirements.
sets: Energy requirements vary with factors including age

subject: Biology
text: Which reagent is used to test for starch?
explain: Iodine solution changes from orange-brown to blue-black when starch is present.
sets: Human nutrition

subject: Biology
text: Describe the positive result of the Benedict's test for reducing sugars.
sets: When heated with a reducing sugar
column14: Benedict's solution changes from blue to a range of colours depending on concentration.

subject: Biology
text: Describe the positive result of the Biuret test for protein.
sets: A positive Biuret test changes from blue to lilac or purple

subject: Biology
text: How is a food sample tested for lipids using the ethanol emulsion test?
answer: add ethanol and shake then add water|shake with ethanol then add water
sets: Lipids dissolve in ethanol. Adding water produces a cloudy white emulsion if lipids are present.

subject: Biology
text: Where does most digestion and absorption of food take place?
explain: The small intestine is adapted for digestion and absorption of soluble nutrients.
sets: Human nutrition

subject: Biology
text: What is the function of the oesophagus?
answer: moves food to the stomach|transports food to the stomach
sets: The oesophagus transports food from the mouth to the stomach using peristalsis.

subject: Biology
text: The physical breakdown of food into smaller pieces is called ___ digestion.
sets: Mechanical digestion increases the surface area of food for enzyme action.

subject: Biology
text: Describe how peristalsis moves food through the digestive system.
answer: waves of contraction and relaxation of circular and longitudinal muscles|muscles contract behind food and relax in front
sets: Peristalsis involves coordinated contractions and relaxations of muscles in the gut wall to push food along.

subject: Biology
text: Which enzyme breaks down starch into maltose?
explain: Amylase catalyses the breakdown of starch into maltose.
sets: Human nutrition

subject: Biology
text: State the substrate and product of protease activity.
answer: protein and amino acids|proteins and amino acids
sets: Proteases break down proteins into amino acids.

subject: Biology
text: What are the products of lipid digestion?
answer: fatty acids and glycerol|fatty acids plus glycerol
sets: Lipases break down lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.

subject: Biology
text: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.
sets: Enzymes increase reaction rates without being used up in the reaction.

subject: Biology
text: Explain why an enzyme stops working if its active site changes shape.
answer: substrate no longer fits active site|enzyme and substrate cannot form an enzyme-substrate complex
sets: A change in the active site's shape prevents the substrate from binding
column14: so the enzyme cannot catalyse the reaction effectively.

subject: Biology
text: Explain why very high temperatures reduce enzyme activity.
answer: bonds maintaining enzyme structure break|active site changes shape|enzyme becomes denatured|substrate no longer fits
sets: High temperatures disrupt bonds maintaining the enzyme's structure. The active site changes shape and the enzyme becomes denatured.

subject: Biology
text: State two adaptations of villi for efficient absorption.
answer: large surface area|thin epithelium|rich blood supply|many microvilli
sets: Villi provide a large surface area
column14: have a thin epithelial layer and contain many capillaries for rapid absorption.

subject: Biology
text: Explain how the structure of a villus helps it absorb digested nutrients efficiently.
answer: Large surface area|thin wall|good blood supply|maintains concentration gradient|lacteal absorbs fatty acids and glycerol
model: 1 mark: Large surface area from villi and microvilli. 1 mark: Epithelium is one cell thick, giving a short diffusion distance. 1 mark: Rich blood supply carries absorbed nutrients away and maintains a concentration gradient. 1 mark: Lacteal absorbs products of lipid digestion.
explain: The villus has a large surface area because of its shape and microvilli. Its epithelium is thin
sets: allowing a short diffusion distance. A rich blood supply maintains concentration gradients and transports nutrients away. Lacteals absorb products of lipid digestion.

subject: Biology
text: Where is bile produced?
explain: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder.
sets: Human nutrition

subject: Biology
text: State two functions of bile in digestion.
answer: neutralises stomach acid|emulsifies fats|increases surface area of lipids
sets: Bile neutralises acidic chyme from the stomach and emulsifies lipids into smaller droplets
column14: increasing the surface area for lipase action.

subject: Biology
text: What is the main function of the large intestine?
answer: absorbs water|absorption of water from undigested food
sets: The large intestine absorbs water from undigested material

subject: Biology
text: Describe the journey of food through the digestive system and explain where digestion and absorption occur.
model: 1 mark: Food is ingested and mechanically broken down in the mouth. 1 mark: Amylase begins starch digestion in the mouth. 1 mark: Food passes down the oesophagus by peristalsis and proteins are digested in the stomach by protease. 1 mark: Digestion is completed in the small intestine by enzymes. 1 mark: Digested nutrients are absorbed through villi in the small intestine and water is absorbed in the large intestine.
explain: Food is ingested and mechanically broken down in the mouth
sets: where amylase begins starch digestion. It travels down the oesophagus by peristalsis to the stomach
column14: where proteases digest proteins. Digestion is completed in the small intestine by enzymes. Nutrients are absorbed through the villi of the small intestine
column15: while water is absorbed in the large intestine.
